key_insight: Cube-and-halo decomposition scales the universal ALIGNN-FF force field to billion-atom energy and force evaluations on desk-side GPUs.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes experimentally relevant structures accessible to individual research groups without requiring a supercomputing cluster.
method: Partition the atomic structure into cubes for separate evaluation.
Include halo atoms spanning the model’s full 20 Å receptive field to preserve exact results.
Distribute cube evaluations across memory-limited desk-side GPUs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 2-billion-atom evaluation on nine NVIDIA GB10s and demonstrations on a billion-atom polycrystal, a 102-million-atom gate stack, and a 1.07-million-atom virus-in-water system.
watch_item: The reported scale concerns single-point evaluations; it does not establish practical molecular-dynamics throughput or force-field accuracy across all demonstrated systems.
paper_title: Scaling a Universal Graph Neural Network Force Field to Billions of Atoms on Desk-Side GPUs
